text.p: The Indonesian military has revoked shoot-on-sight orders announced in Jakarta after riots in July, the Jakarta Post newspaper said on Saturday.
"We issued the order for a limited period of time only," Jakarta military commander Major-General Sutiyoso was quoted as saying.
The order was no longer needed because further large-scale violence was unlikely, Sutiyoso said.
Troops were ordered to shoot on sight to prevent a recurrence of riots in the city that began on July 27.
At least five people died in the violence, the worst in Jakarta for more than two decades, and scores of buildings and vehicles were set ablaze.
Armed soldiers were deployed around the city following the riots but were withdrawn at the end of last month.
The riots started after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), which supporters of ousted leader Megawati Sukarnoputri refused to vacate.
Megawati loyalists occupied the building after a government-funded congress of PDI rebels in Medan, North Sumatra, in June elected deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi as party leader.
Megawati, daughter of late founding president Sukarno, said the move was unconstitutional and illegal as she had been elected PDI leader for a five-year term in 1993.
A lawsuit filed by Megawati against the government has been adjourned until later this month.
